coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Parcel K South (PKS)
record.summary: The southern piece of the Port's 20th/Illinois Street parcel, on Illinois Street south of the new 21st Street, reserved under the 2017 approvals as a 100%-affordable housing site (65 ft under the D4D). The Port's 2026 report assigns it to Phase 2 and says its gap funding is not yet available; no developer has been selected.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4110013, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. That this is the lot of Parcel K South is Pier & Point's own inference from location, shape and size (our earlier trace of the D4D figure measured 1,709 m2 against the lot's 1,637 m2; 83% of the trace lies inside the lot and the trace covers 86% of it). No Port document read ties the lot number to it. A building may sit back from the lot lines. None of the sources read reports construction, a developer or a start date for this block. Port Item 11A (Aug 7, 2026) places Parcel K South in Phase 2 of the project and says that funding for the 100% affordable sites is 'currently unavailable as market-rate development has yet to occur'; its statement that 'construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward' concerns Phase 1 of the 28-Acre Site, not this parcel. It is Parcel K South, a Port-retained parcel created from the Port's Illinois & 20th Street Parcel (Port Item 9B, Res 17-52), outside the 28-Acre Site and the developer's vertical option; Port Item 9B gives that parent parcel as Block 4110 Lot 001, which DataSF lists as retired 2018-10-02.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4110013 (recorded 2019-02-07; mapped 2019-03-14; active); cross-checked against Pier 70 Design for Development Figure 6.4.2 - Building Height Maximum (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No single Assessor lot is documented as Parcel K South. Lot 4110013 (active) matches its location, shape and size, so its outline is Assessor lot 4110013; the identification is Pier & Point's inference, as the accuracy note says.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential in every D4D land-use scenario (Figures 1.5.5-1.5.7), 65 ft max per Figure 6.4.2, and a 100%-affordable housing site under Port Item 9B. A real parcel distinct from Parcel K North: Port Resolution 17-52 (Item 9B, Sept 2017) has the Port subdivide the 20th/Illinois parcel into four parcels including Parcel K North and Parcel K South, and the Port's Item 12B memo (Feb 2020) names 'the Illinois/20th Street parcels known as Parcel K North and Parcel K South' (its Resolution 20-07 recital says 'the Illinois/20th Street parcel known as Parcel K', singular). No source found gives a specific unit count, architect, or construction-status beyond this.

facts.value: 100% affordable housing (one of three stand-alone affordable parcels with C1B and C2A)
Port of San Francisco (Port-controlled parcel outside the developer's option)
no more than six residential stories (D4D S6.4.2)
Phase 2 (affordable) / Phase 2B in Exhibit A, with C1 (Port's 2026 report)
At least 30% affordable under the 2017 plan; the 2026 proposal lowers the project-wide rate to no less than 20%, keeping a 327-unit minimum
HDY3 and HDY1/2 may combine Retail and Service frontage on 22nd Street (D4D); Irish Hill Corner Plaza lies between them, not at PKS

milestones.text: Resolution of Intention to form Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District No. 2 (Hoedown Yard), to finance affordable housing within Pier 70 and Parcel K South, introduced at the Board of Supervisors (File 170880; Port Item 9B says July 25, 2017 in its text and 7/27/17 in its Table 9). Item 9B says the resolution calls a hearing for October 24, 2017, but the Board's record shows the file passed on July 26, 2018 (Resolution 234-18) with a title that calls the hearing for September 11, 2018, so the October 2017 hearing date was not kept; whether the district has been formed is not established here

changes.text: The 2026-10-06 entry for this record said the 2033 date comes from the Development Agreement's Schedule of Performance. That was wrong. The Port's 2017 staff report (Item 9B, p.7) puts the Schedule of Performance in the Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA) between the Port and the developer, which is a different agreement from the Development Agreement between the City and the developer. The report says the developer must complete phase 2 within 16 years of project approval, but it never states the year 2033; 2033 is Pier & Point's own arithmetic (2017 plus 16 years). It stays labelled a legal outside date, not an expected completion.
